original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-surjective-flat-locally-finite-presentation}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F, G : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be sheaves.
Let $a : F \to G$ be representable by algebraic spaces, flat,
locally of finite presentation, and surjective.
Then $a : F \to G$ is surjective as a map of sheaves.

final_content.statement:
A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

semantic_review_note: Pinned bootstrap.tex L378–392 defines flatness, surjectivity and locally finite presentation via every algebraic-space base change. Original L590–597 requires both F,G to be fppf sheaves and a to have all these properties, then concludes surjectivity as a map of sheaves (fppf-local lifting), not global-section surjectivity; the proposal retains that exact distinction.
